A_target.statement:
Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be [[Definition:Independent Random Variables|independent]] with [[Definition:Survival Function|survival functions]] $S_i$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {\min_i X_i > x} = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map {S_i} x$
In particular, the minimum of independent exponential variables with rates $\lambda_i$ is exponential with rate $\sum_i \lambda_i$.

B_source.statement:
Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be independent with [[Definition:Cumulative Distribution Function|distribution functions]] $F_i$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {\max_i X_i \le x} = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map {F_i} x$

derived.the product formula: the survival function of the minimum

object_map.reformulation: Exchange maximum with minimum and lower with upper events; both become intersections of independent events.

validity_conditions: Independence of the X_i gives independence of the events {X_i > x}.
The exponential case uses S_i(x) = exp(-lambda_i x).
proof_plan: $\set {\max_i X_i \le x} = \bigcap_i \set {X_i \le x}$, and dually $\set {\min_i X_i > x} = \bigcap_i \set {X_i > x}$.
The events $\set {X_i > x}$ are independent, as the $X_i$ are.
Hence, as in the source result, $\map \Pr {\min_i X_i > x} = \displaystyle \prod_i \map \Pr {X_i > x} = \prod_i \map {S_i} x$.

For exponentials, $\displaystyle \prod_i e^{-\lambda_i x} = e^{-\paren {\sum_i \lambda_i} x}$, the survival function of an exponential with rate $\sum_i \lambda_i$.
{{qed}}
